title: MiSA Vignette
text: MiSA identifies disease-associated spatial dysbiosis testing whether spatial organization microbial taxa differs clinical groups, using image-based microbiome data. typical analysis follows steps: Preprocessing: identify region study (.e., area colonized microbes) image build observation windows (kde_est(), alpha_windows()). Taxon-level testing: characterize spatial distribution taxon summary function d(r) compare groups using four MiSA variants. Community-level testing: combine taxon-level results assess overall spatial dysbiosis. Step 1 described Preprocessing section, steps 2 3 MiSA test section. Step 1 optional. Users already observation windows images can pass directly estimate_L() running MiSA. step 1 skipped entirely, estimate_L() uses default window: convex hull cell locations. following packages required functions examples MiSA package: ggplot2, grid, harmonicmeanp, spatstat.explore, spatstat.geom, stats, deldir, sf.
code: library(MiSA)

what: Kernel density estimate of cell locations
title: MiSA Vignette
code: img_kde <- kde_est(example_image)  # visualize the distribution of density par(mfrow=c(1,2)) plot(img_kde, main="Kernel Density Estimation") hist(img_kde$v, main = "Distribution of estimated density", xlab = "density") abline(v=0.002, lty=2)

title: MiSA Vignette
text: alpha_windows() builds observation windows around high-density cell regions image. Separated regions kept apart, returned owin object, sorted area largest smallest. alpha controls tightly window follows shape high-density region, units coordinates. Smaller values give tighter, detailed boundary, larger values give smoother one. default 200. set cutoff = 0.002 based histogram estimated densities. Areas kernel density 0.002 excluded analysis. fill_holes = TRUE, holes within region filled, window bounded outer boundary . plot_regions() draws observation window regions single plot, labeled name. also returns union regions single window (owin object), save W_all. separated region returned window, users can use single region combine several (e.g., W <- spatstat.geom::union.owin(wins$region1, wins$region2)) true region study. example, use region1, largest region, region study plot example image.  running MiSA, W can used window image including groupA_window_list groupB_window_list argument estimate_L(). arguments take named list one entry per image, names match image IDs, e.g. groupA_window_list <- list("image1" = W, "image2" = NULL, "image3" = NULL, ...). Images set NULL use default window (convex hull cell locations).
code: wins <- alpha_windows(img_kde, alpha = 200, cutoff = 0.002, fill_holes = TRUE) #>          region region_area #> region1 region1    28766056 #> region2 region2      193402 par(mfrow=c(1,2)) W_all <- plot_regions(wins)  W <- wins$region1 plot(example_image$x, example_image$y, pch=20, col="pink", cex=0.1, main = "Microbial map with study region (W)", xlab = "", ylab = "") plot(W, add = TRUE, lwd = 2)

text: estimate_d takes estimated LL curves groupA groupB input, outputs estimated dd curve group label (groupA groupB) image. Visualize dd curves individual taxon, colored groups.
code: d_result <- estimate_d(groupA_L = L_result$groupA_L, groupB_L = L_result$groupB_L, taxa = taxa_all,r_vec = r_all) #> calculating d for Capnocytophaga  #> calculating d for Pasteurellaceae  #> calculating d for Campylobacter  #> calculating d for Leptotrichia  #> calculating d for Neisseriaceae  #> calculating d for Corynebacterium  #> calculating d for Gemella  #> calculating d for Fusobacterium  #> calculating d for Actinomyces  #> calculating d for Lautropia par(mfrow=c(2,5)) for (taxon in taxa_all){   d.mat <- d_result[[taxon]]   r <- as.numeric(colnames(d.mat$d))   matplot(r, t(d.mat$d), type = "l", lty = 1, col = ifelse(d.mat$group =="groupB", "red","black"), main=taxon, ylab = "d", xlab="r") }

title: MiSA Vignette
text: MiSA_data function prepares dd curves MiSA test. Within taxon, first filters images limited spatial range, .e., images whose dd curve valid values radius threshold, r_thresh. default (r_thresh = NULL), dd curves reach 0.5×0.5 \timesmax(r_all) excluded. Users may set r_thresh based scientific question interest; example, r_thresh = 500 exclude dd curves valid estimates r=500r=500. curves kept, function truncates estimated dd curves maximum rr shared common across images (groups) taxon. MiSA_check drops taxa valid hypothesis testing via MiSA, based following criteria: one group remains filtering. total sample size ≤2\leq 2. dd one fewer valid estimates. Use following code visualize dd curves prepared hypothesis testing.
code: data_pre <- MiSA_data(est_d = d_result, r_thresh = NULL) data_checked <- MiSA_check(data_list = data_pre) par(mfrow=c(2,5)) for (taxon in taxa_all){   d.mat <- data_checked[[taxon]]   r <- as.numeric(colnames(d.mat$d))   matplot(r, t(d.mat$d), type = "l", lty = 1, col = ifelse(d.mat$group =="groupB", "red","black"), main=taxon, ylab = "d", xlab="r") }

title: Test for differential spatial patterns using MiSA — MiSA
text: Four tests available via method argument: "orig" Evaluates raw statistic \(d(r)\) (capturing magnitude direction deviation CSR) set pre-selected radii, combines resulting p-values across radii using harmonic mean p-value (HMP) method. "abs" Similar "orig", compares absolute value \(d(r)\) (capturing magnitude deviation) selected radii instead. "sup" Evaluates maximum absolute deviation, \(\max_r |d(r)|\), capturing signals may arise spatial scale. "area" Evaluates integrated magnitude deviation \(d(r)\) across full range radii, capturing signals may arise spatial scale. "orig" "abs", radii used can specified via omnibus_r omnibus_num. omnibus_r specified, function always uses omnibus_r, regardless input omnibus_num. omnibus_r left default (NULL) omnibus_num specified, function uses omnibus_num evenly spaced radii instead. omnibus_r omnibus_num left defaults (NULL), function sets omnibus_num = min(5, c - 1), c number radii available taxon. function uses whichever group entered groupA (data preparation) reference group. negative effect size indicates summary statistic smaller reference group comparison group, indicating comparison group spatially structured (e.g., exhibiting stronger clustering regularity) relative reference group.
